summary.name: Libervia (Salut à Toi)
summary.one_liner: Libervia, formerly Salut à Toi, is a multipurpose, multi-frontend, decentralised XMPP-based communication tool written in Python, covered in this 2026 progress note.
use_cases: chatting and making audio/video calls over XMPP
reading email inside an XMPP client
hosting a git repository browser with tickets
running XMPP without a central server
installing a Python XMPP backend with uv
summary.what_it_does: The page is a 2026 progress note from the Libervia developer describing recent work on the project. Libervia has audio/video support, including direct calls, MUJI mesh group calls, and SFU-based conferences using Galène, plus experimental remote desktop control. It includes an email gateway that maps mailing lists to XMPP forums, and a new built-in Forge for browsing git repositories and XMPP-based tickets. The author describes moving settings to TOML with Pydantic Settings, replacing Wokkel with the Tx-XMPP fork, and adding a pubsub component with node relationships. The web frontend is being redesigned on Brython and Jinja templates, and work on Tor access and serverless XMPP is in progress under an NLnet grant.
notable: Installable with a single uv one-liner from git, replacing the old Mercurial repository with a built-in Git forge
Built-in pubsub implementation supporting XEP-0496 node relationships and XEP-0499 extended discovery
Email gateway that converts mailing lists into XMPP forums
Settings moved to libervia.toml with Pydantic validation and automatic bridge fallback from D-Bus to Perspective Broker
caveats: Libervia is a solo-developer project, and the author says resources are limited
Web frontend is not yet fully usable; an alpha release is planned but not released
SFU remote desktop control is described as really experimental
Term-image was disabled and Mercurial-to-Git and pubsub feature parity are still incomplete; the merge request system is not yet integrated into the forge
